result.summary: In 2026 Musk kept giving short AI timelines. At the 1 September G20 meeting he said AI will do anything digital by the end of 2027 and be unbeatable at software 'next year'. In the 23 July Economist interview he said AI will pass the combined intelligence of all humans in about five years. The Moonshots 'AGI in 2026' remark was recorded in December 2025, so it belongs to 2025. I did not reach the recorded January Davos claim or the Optimus claims on any page I opened.

reply_text:
I found three 2026 predictions I can quote from pages I opened, plus one I only saw as a news paraphrase. None of them repeats your three recorded claims, which I didn't come across on any opened page.

- **G20 Innovation Ministerial, Chapel Hill, 1 September 2026 (published transcript).** Musk said AI will do "anything digital" "probably by the end of next year". He said AI software will be "Stockfish-level" good "next year", so a person can't compete with it. He said it will be "extremely good" at vision and anything digital "literally in twelve to eighteen months". He also said there will be over a billion humanoid robots in ten years, producing more than all humans combined. The robot line is about Optimus-type robots, not AI as such, so you may want to drop it.
- **The Economist interview, recorded 23 July 2026 (transcript).** He said AI may exceed the sum of human intelligence in "roughly five years". He also said humans being in control in ten years is "unlikely", but the ten-year span was in the interviewer's question, not his own words.
- **Forbes award appearance, about May 2026 (coverage only).** A Not a Tesla App article reports he said AI will be smarter than humans "within one to two years", with no direct quote from him. Treat it as a lead until someone checks the video.

**What I left out:**
- **Moonshots podcast:** the transcripts say January 6, 2026, but the show notes say it was recorded on 22 December 2025. So its "AGI in 2026" line counts for 2025. I didn't see that line on either page I opened, so I haven't quoted it.
- **Forbes, 24 September 2026:** the article says SpaceX's AI could pass OpenAI and Anthropic "in about 6 months", but only the headline and summary loaded, so I couldn't read his words.

I used 6 of 12 searches and all 6 page openings. One search was used up by a coding error. The Moonshots transcript was cut off before its AGI timeline section, and the Economist transcript ended mid-sentence, so both may hold more.
